plan.contextChunk: This figure has two panels, (a) and (b), each drawing a convex polygon over labeled points in the plane. In (a) a light gray polygon labeled Q_j fills the right portion; its boundary runs from p_0 at the bottom left up to p_j at the top, right through p_k and two unlabeled black dots, down the right side to p_2, and back along the bottom through p_1 to p_0. A darker gray triangle is attached along the left, with corners p_0, p_j, and a further point p_i lying outside to the left, so that the two shaded regions together form a larger polygon whose boundary now passes through p_i. In (b) the hull boundary is a thick gray chain from p_0 rightward to p_1, up the right side, and back across the top through p_j; at the left a thin-outlined light gray triangle has corners p_i, p_r just to its right, and p_0 at the bottom, and a point p_t sits inside that triangle. Dashed segments join p_i and p_r to p_t, and a small arc marks the angle at p_t. Placing the panels side by side contrasts a point that enlarges the hull with a point enclosed by three others and therefore incapable of being a hull vertex. The pair underpins the correctness argument for Graham's scan, where each newly considered point either joins the stack or forces an earlier point off it.

interactionPlan.concept: In Graham's scan, the turn direction at the top of the stack decides hull membership: a left turn extends the hull to include the new point, while a nonleft turn proves the middle point lies inside a triangle of other points and must be popped.

interactions.label: Case

interactions.teaches: How Graham's scan incrementally maintains the hull: each candidate is tested against the top two stack points, then pushed or the offending point is popped.
interactions.label: Step the scan

interactions.teaches: Which specific triple of points certifies a point's status — the two supporting hull vertices for an accepted point, or the three enclosing points for an interior point.
interactions.teachesDetail: Clicking p_i, p_j, p_r, or p_t highlights that point and its supporting triangle or hull edge.

demo_steps.title: The hull so far
demo_steps.narration: The light gray polygon Q_j is the convex hull of the points processed so far, with p_0 at the bottom and the stack running counterclockwise to p_j. Everything already accepted is a vertex of this shape.

demo_steps.title: Testing a left turn
demo_steps.narration: The next candidate p_i is tested against the top two stack points. The turn from p_0→p_j to p_j→p_i is a left turn, so p_i lies outside the current hull.

demo_steps.title: Push: the hull grows
demo_steps.narration: p_i is pushed onto the stack and the dark triangle p_0–p_j–p_i is annexed to Q_j. The boundary now detours through p_i, showing that a left turn strictly enlarges the hull.

demo_steps.title: A nonleft turn
demo_steps.narration: Switch to panel (b). Here the angle at p_t formed by p_i, p_t, p_r is not a left turn — the dashed segments and the arc show p_t bending the wrong way.

demo_steps.title: Pop: the point was never a vertex
demo_steps.narration: Because the turn is nonleft, p_t lies inside triangle p_i p_r p_0, whose three corners are all hull points. A point interior to a triangle of hull points cannot be a hull vertex, so p_t is popped.

demo_steps.title: Two cases, one test
demo_steps.narration: Side by side, the panels show the invariant: every candidate either extends the boundary outward or reveals an earlier point as interior. Nothing else can happen.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A nonleft turn is not just a bookkeeping rule — it is geometric proof that the middle point lies strictly inside a triangle formed by three other hull points, so it can never be a vertex of the convex hull.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Two side-by-side panels on a white background, labeled (a) and (b) in italic beneath each. Panel (a): a light gray filled convex polygon occupying the right two-thirds, its interior labeled 'Q_j' in italic serif; vertices marked as small filled black dots with italic serif labels p_0 (bottom left), p_j (top), p_k (upper right of p_j), two unlabeled dots along the upper-right chain, p_2 (right side), p_1 (bottom right). A medium/dark gray triangle p_0–p_j–p_i is attached on the left, with p_i protruding further left; the shared chord p_0–p_j is drawn as a thin line so the two shaded regions read as distinct. The outer boundary of the combined shape is a thick light-gray stroke. Panel (b): the same overall hull silhouette but unfilled — only a thick gray boundary chain from p_0 (bottom left) rightward to p_1, up the right side through unlabeled dots, and across the top through p_j. At the left sits a narrow light-gray triangle with thin black outline, corners p_i (upper left), p_r (to its right), p_0 (bottom); inside it a dot p_t with dashed segments to p_i and p_r and a small arc at p_t marking the angle. For the demo, use a saturated accent color (e.g. orange) for the currently tested angle arc and triple, and a muted red for a popped point; add a small stack readout strip under each panel showing stack contents bottom-to-top. Keep all labels italic serif in the style of CLRS.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Toggle between the left-turn case in panel (a) and the nonleft-turn case in panel (b): the candidate point either expands the shaded hull or is shown inside the triangle, making clear how turn direction determines hull membership.
- Button for stepping through the Graham-scan stack update: each press tests the next labeled point, draws the relevant angle, and either pushes the point or removes the interior point, making clear why nonleft turns cannot remain on the convex hull.
- Click for p_i, p_j, p_r, or p_t: the selected point and its supporting triangle or hull edge highlight, making clear which surrounding points prove that it belongs on or inside the hull.

authoredContext: Theorem 33.1 (Correctness of Graham’s scan) If GRAHAM-SCAN executes on a set Q of points, where jQj _x0015_ 3, then at termination, the stack S consists of, from bottom to top, exactly the vertices of CH.Q/ in counterclockwise order. Proof After line 2, we have the sequence of points hp1; p2; : : : ; pmi. Let us define, for i D 2; 3; : : : ; m, the subset of points Qi D fp0; p1; : : : ; pi g. The points in Q Qm are those that were removed because they had the same polar angle relative to p0 as some point in Qm; these points are not in CH.Q/, and so CH.Qm/ D CH.Q/. Thus, it suffices to show that when GRAHAM-SCAN terminates, the stack S consists of the vertices of CH.Qm/ in counterclockwise order, when listed from bottom to top. Note that just as p0, p1, and pm are vertices of CH.Q/, the points p0, p1, and pi are all vertices of CH.Qi/. The proof uses the following loop invariant: At the start of each iteration of the for loop of lines 9–12, stack S consists of, from bottom to top, exactly the vertices of CH.Qi1/ in counterclockwise order

discrepancies: Label typography: the italic base letter and its subscript are rendered as separate text elements with a visible gap (reads as 'p j', 'p i', 'Q j') instead of a tight subscript as in the source.

Overall label size is a bit small relative to the source — at inline scale the viewBox (860×390) shrinks the 17px labels to ~11px and the panel captions '(a)'/'(b)' to ~10px, noticeably smaller/lighter than the prominent serif labels of the original.

In panel (b) the generated figure draws dashed segments both pᵢ→pₜ and pᵣ→pₜ; the source shows essentially one faint dashed segment plus the small angle arc at pₜ, so the added dashed leg is a mild embellishment.
Minor: the anchor/vertex dots are slightly smaller and the thick hull stroke marginally thinner than in the source, making the grey boundary read a touch lighter.
evaluation.notes: A near drop-in reproduction of both panels with correct polygon topology, shaded Qⱼ, annexed dark triangle, the pᵢpᵣp₀ certificate triangle and angle arc, backed by a genuinely useful 6-step scan demo, case toggle, step/reset buttons and click-to-explain points; only label typography (split subscripts) and overall label size fall short.

feedback.rationale: No failure modes or action items remain and all core dimensions score 4.7–5, with only minor typographic/sizing nitpicks that don't warrant another iteration.
